known_differences_from_fetch_script: The layer carries records of two other agencies under their own case-number series: 'A' + year (e.g. A23-0227; 5,233 rows matching ^A\d, 2018-2024 only) at Algona addresses (Warde St, Milwaukee Ave N, Algona Blvd) and 'YY-P####' / '25P08####' (4,904 rows matching ^\d{2}-?P\d) at Pacific addresses (Valentine Ave SE, Stewart Rd SW, Frontage Rd N) (query.py on raw_cache; avg latitude 47.282 and 47.265 vs 47.306 for the other rows). Official totals are for Auburn's ORI WA0170100 only (evidence/official_totals.csv official_basis) and Auburn city is the only scope candidate (evidence/scope_candidates.csv), so every rule excludes both series on CASENUMBER. Without the exclusion, 330 in-year mapped rows are Algona/Pacific and about 155 of them fall in block groups the crosswalk assigns to Auburn city (the prior run's footprint step dropped only 179 of 5,845 in-state mapped rows; evidence/funnel.csv), including Pacific homicides 20-P0612 (234 Stewart Road SE) and 23-P0916 (1446 Valentine Ave SE). With the exclusion, the footprint step drops 4 of 5,515 in-state mapped rows (cc.funnel on the archived pull). If Auburn PD were shown to report these cities under its ORI the scope would instead have to add them; the separate numbering and the single-ORI totals point to exclusion.

Larceny and motor vehicle theft are unmapped. OFFENSE has a single theft category ('Theft', 'THEFT', each also with trailing-space padding; evidence/raw_cache_profile.json) and no other published field (REPORTED, CASENUMBER, address, REPORTING_DISTRICT, OFFENSE; evidence/doc_87bcbedc2c.json fields) separates vehicle theft from other larceny. Theft run through the same contract (Algona/Pacific excluded, located, in footprint, deduplicated), 2018-2025: 2570, 2518, 2726, 3128, 3434, 2479, 1910, 1453. That is 1.02x-1.57x official larceny alone (2118, 2030, 2152, 2285, 2188, 2033, 1806, 1426) and 0.94x-1.00x official larceny plus motor vehicle theft (2731, 2550, 2812, 3140, 3458) for 2018-2022, 0.67x-0.78x (3567, 2848, 1872) for 2023-2025 (evidence/official_totals.csv). The category straddles 23A-23H and 240 and is left out rather than mapped to either.

Aggravated assault is unmapped: 'Assault' (with trailing-space variant; evidence/raw_cache_profile.json) has no aggravated/simple split. Through the same contract steps its counts are 849, 945, 924, 951, 906, 810, 825, 760 for 2018-2025, 3.26x (2024, 825/253) to 6.39x (2025, 760/119) official aggravated assault, so it is mostly 13B simple assault. 'Threats' and 'Weapons Offense' are not mapped either.

Rape is unmapped: the only sexual category is 'Sex Offense' (evidence/raw_cache_profile.json), which cannot separate 11A-11C from 11D fondling and other sex offenses. Through the same contract steps: 150, 166, 134, 153, 134, 95, 119, 154 for 2018-2025, 1.63x (2024, 119/73) to 3.39x (2019, 166/49) official rape.

'Homicide' is mapped to murder but is an undefined publisher summary category that may include negligent manslaughter (09B) or justifiable homicide (09C); death investigations are a separate 'Dead Body' category. With the Algona/Pacific exclusion (which removes the two Pacific homicides), deduplicated footprint counts 2018-2025 are 6, 5, 10, 5, 14, 12, 5, 3 (60) vs official murder 1, 4, 8, 4, 13, 8, 10, 3 (51; evidence/official_totals.csv).

Robbery and burglary are coarse categories taken as 120 and 220 without a published crosswalk. Deduplicated footprint counts 2018-2025 with the exclusion (cc.funnel): burglary 588, 540, 568, 615, 866, 701, 389, 226 vs official 605, 480, 584, 595, 883, 846, 439, 242 (0.83x in 2023 to 1.13x in 2019); robbery 113, 120, 123, 132, 115, 187, 107, 58 vs official 121, 117, 121, 136, 125, 210, 114, 61 (0.89x in 2023 to 1.03x in 2019).

The date is the report date (REPORTED is the only date field, evidence/doc_87bcbedc2c.json); no occurrence date is published, so incidents reported in a later year than they occurred fall in the report year.

Each row carries one OFFENSE; the feed publishes one summary category per case number, not the NIBRS offense list or SRS hierarchy, so an incident with several Part I offenses contributes only its published category.

Uncategorized rows grow in the last three years: OFFENSE blank or '-' on 4, 12, 52, 48, 34, 655, 1050, 2688 rows for 2018-2025 (query.py, trim(OFFENSE) IN ('','-')), while total rows fall from 18,156 (2018) to 11,753 (2025). These rows cannot be mapped and are a likely contributor to the 2023-2025 shortfalls against official totals.
notes: Source: the survey's single ArcGIS layer 'Crimes' (evidence/registry_row.json api_endpoint, portal_type arcgis_feature_service; evidence/doc_87bcbedc2c.json name 'Crimes', maxRecordCount 2000, so page_size 2000 and order OBJECTID ASC). The landing page (evidence/doc_1a90542764.html) holds only 'TEST'. The where clause is the survey's probe_where and the archive's filter (packet.json case_text). Dates: REPORTED (esriFieldTypeDate) is the only date field and is the report date; no occurrence date is published. It is epoch ms; the pull spans 2018-01-01 00:02:55 to 2025-12-31 23:05:00 read as UTC (query.py, make_timestamp(REPORTED*1000)), matching the where bounds. The layer declares datesInUnknownTimezone false, but the hour-of-day profile read as UTC has its trough at 03:00-05:00 (2,423-2,530 rows) and peak at 12:00 (6,990), which fits local wall-clock time stored without offset, so the UTC year of the epoch is the local year; year_field is empty and year comes from REPORTED with date_format epoch_ms. Unit and id: count_unit incident, per the survey (evidence/registry_row.json count_unit). One row per case: 120,558 rows and 120,381 distinct trimmed CASENUMBER values (query.py; the runner trims ids). Case-number series (query.py, digit-shape patterns): 'YY-NNNNN' (95,961 rows, Auburn), 'YY-E#####' (10,611; plus 105 'YYE######' in 2025), 'YY-S#####' (2,545, mostly trespass at retail addresses), a 9-digit series (1,103, almost all 2025, e.g. 25008xxxx), 'A' + year (Algona) and 'YY-P####' / '25P08####' (Pacific), plus about 150 malformed or other-format entries. Of the 164 case numbers with more than one row, 140 are exact repeats (same OFFENSE and REPORTED) and 18 carry two different OFFENSE values; dedupe_on_id keeps the first row per case number (lowest OBJECTID in archive order). Offense rules: whole-value matches on OFFENSE via case-insensitive regex that tolerates the trailing-space padding in the pull ('Burglary', 'BURGLARY', 'Robbery', 'Homicide', each also padded; evidence/raw_cache_profile.json). Mapped: Homicide -> murder, Robbery -> robbery, Burglary -> burglary. Each rule excludes CASENUMBER matching ^\s*A\d (Algona) or ^\s*\d{2}-?P\d (Pacific); the regex op is a case-insensitive search (src/crimerisk/city_contracts.py _condition_mask). This removes 330 in-year mapped rows; the revised contract keeps 5,518 in-year mapped rows, 5,511 in the footprint and 5,508 after deduplication (cc.funnel on the archived pull with state/geometry/block_group_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk.parquet). Unmapped because the source cannot separate the FBI offense: Theft (larceny plus motor vehicle theft), Assault (no aggravated/simple split), Sex Offense (rape not separable from fondling). Other categories (Recovered Stole, Impounded Vehic, Fraud, FORG, EMBZ, Arson, Vandalism, Kidnapping, etc.) are not among the seven offenses. Coordinates: the feature geometry (__arcgis_latitude/__arcgis_longitude; source spatial reference WKID 102748 / 2285, evidence/doc_87bcbedc2c.json). The publisher states no rounding or offset; there are 25,005 distinct 6-decimal points for 30,252 distinct addresses among 120,497 located rows, and addresses are full street addresses rather than hundred blocks ('BLOCK' appears in 45 addresses case-insensitively, 9 case-sensitively), so points look like address geocodes. 61 rows have no geometry and 170 located rows fall outside a rough Washington box (lat 45.5-49.1, lon -124.9 to -116.9); these drop at the coordinate or block-group step. Geography: Auburn Police Department is a municipal PD (ORI WA0170100; evidence/registry_row.json), so the scope is Auburn city, 53:municipal:place:5303180, the single candidate in evidence/scope_candidates.csv; Auburn lies in King and Pierce counties, Washington (state_fips 53). The Algona and Pacific series are excluded by case number rather than by widening the scope (see known differences). Exclusions: the layer description and copyrightText are empty and the survey records no redactions (evidence/doc_87bcbedc2c.json; evidence/registry_row.json redactions ''), so no publisher exclusions are listed. Yearly counts of raw rows are from query.py with year(make_timestamp(REPORTED*1000)); offense counts against official totals are deduplicated footprint counts from cc.funnel on the archived pull.
